episode_title: cbuzz: Building a Business People Love with Letha Pugh & Wendy Miller Pugh of Bake Me Happy
question: When did Bake Me Happy start and how many gluten-free bakeries existed in Columbus at that time?
transcript_excerpt: Bake Me Happy started in 2013. When they began, there were approximately four gluten-free bakeries in Columbus, including Holiday in Worthington, Cherbourg, and a bread company. Now there are only two remaining.

episode_title: cbuzz: Building a Business People Love with Letha Pugh & Wendy Miller Pugh of Bake Me Happy
question: What gluten-free recreation products does Bake Me Happy offer as core items?
transcript_excerpt: Bake Me Happy's core nostalgic items include oatmeal cream clouds (like oatmeal cream pies), king dongs, zebra cakes, and pop tarts. They also offer creative riffs on popular items like a spicy peanut butter cookie made with Kremas hot and spicy peanut butter. Their original spongy item (Twinkie recreation) was retired because it was too expensive to make and required touching seven times per item.

episode_title: cbuzz: Building a Business People Love with Letha Pugh & Wendy Miller Pugh of Bake Me Happy
question: What percentage of Preston's sales are gluten-free products through the Bake Me Happy partnership?
transcript_excerpt: Approximately 30 to 35 percent of Preston's sales are gluten-free products through the Bake Me Happy partnership. This natural progression has been beneficial for both companies, with Bake Me Happy winning and Preston's winning as well.

episode_title: cbuzz: Building a Business People Love with Letha Pugh & Wendy Miller Pugh of Bake Me Happy
question: How long have Bake Me Happy's longest-serving staff members been with the company?
transcript_excerpt: Bake Me Happy, which is 13 to 14 years old, has three staff members who have been with the company for almost 10 years, and two staff members who have been with them for almost eight years. This long tenure in food service is attributed to their careful interview process and focus on brand alignment and loyalty.

episode_title: cbuzz: Building a Business People Love with Letha Pugh & Wendy Miller Pugh of Bake Me Happy
question: What is Letha Pugh's approach to addressing barriers to employment in the hospitality industry?
transcript_excerpt: Letha Pugh emphasizes that Bake Me Happy pays employees well as part of being responsible business owners. She is launching The Line through Service, which focuses on the hospitality industry and valuing employees appropriately. She highlights that the hospitality pay scale based on minimum wage plus tips is unsustainable given rising rents and cost of living.
